title: introduce-inference-econ-decision-tree-suggester
author: Priya Singh
description: Summary: Adds a small, auditable decision-tree based suggester service that consumes recent tenant telemetry and workload shapes to recommend safe defaults for batching, prefix/KV cache window, and quantization profile tiers. Motivation: customers frequently ask for one-click recommendations that reduce token cost without regressing latency or quality. The heuristic presets in Optimize are useful but brittle for mixed workloads; this PR introduces an explainable decision tree that maps telemetry signatures (median seq length, 95th latency, KV hit rate, model family, CPU/GPU footprint) to conservative default profiles. Key design goals: 1) deterministic and auditable recommendations, 2) low-cost inference (rules only reference aggregated telemetry, no raw prompts), 3) safe fallbacks and explicit human-readable rationale, 4) incremental rollout and A/B telemetry. What changed (high level): new service under /services/econ-suggester, a small rules engine with exported rationale strings, a CLI dry-run mode for operators, and a set of unit tests and integration harness scenarios. The decision tree is intentionally shallow (max depth 4) and implemented as data (yaml nodes) to allow future non-destructive updates via config. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests for tree evaluation - [x] integration test that runs the suggester against replayed tenant traces - [x] telemetry metrics (suggester.recommendations, suggester.rationale_hash) - [x] CLI dry-run and export to JSON - [x] e2e smoke run on staging - [ ] docs: user-facing guidance and Console integration (follow-up PR) Related: Linear ENG-13023, ENG-13590, infra/ops runbook entry https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-13023 Decision rationale export (example): "tenant: acme-corp, model: rw-1-mt, median_seq: 128 -> recommend: small-batch(8, 32ms-prefill), cache_window: 16kb, quant: q4_0; rationale: 'median_seq between 64-256 and KV hit < 5% suggests short-context batchable calls; choose conservative quant with no red-team to avoid quality regressions'" Commits (summary): - add [econ-suggester] lightweight decision tree evaluator and config loader - add CLI dry-run + replay adapter for trace-based evaluation - export suggester metrics and rationale hash for telemetry - add unit + integration tests - add initial YAML configuration (shallow trees) - add ci matrix job for suggester tests Changed files (high level): - services/econ-suggester/{main.go, tree_evaluator.go, config.yaml} - pkg/telemetry/suggester_metrics.go - tools/suggester-cli/{main.go, README.md} - tests/integration/econ-suggester/{replay_fixtures, smoke_test.go} - deployment/staging/suggester.yaml - Makefile: add suggester test target Review summary: The approach intentionally avoids ML-in-the-loop for the first iteration and focuses on explainability and safe defaults. The output is a JSON recommendation plus an English rationale string suitable for Console display. CI: initial runs flagged a flaky replay test that depended on timing; fixed by adding a deterministic clock to the replay harness. CI status at merge: pass. Merge: squash and merge. Migration/rollout: staged rollout via feature flag (econ.suggester.enabled) and dry-run telemetry to measure uplift before enabling automatic adoption.

review_comments: Lukas Bauer: Nice work. A few nits: please make the rationale strings stable across minor config refactors (hash), and add a test for the case where KV hit rate is high but median seq is short.
Priya Singh: Added rationale_hash metric and a deterministic YAML serializer to keep strings stable. Added the requested test and an integration fixture with high-KV-hit traces.
Noah Chen: Can we ensure the suggester never recommends quant tiers stricter than tenant opt-in? Please gate quant suggestions behind tenant_opt_in flag.

Priya Singh: Updated evaluator to respect tenant opt-in flag; recommender will only emit quant suggestions if tenant.metadata.flags.opt_in_quant == true. Added unit test and updated CLI to show opt-in status.
Ava Martinez: CI flaky on replay fixed by deterministic clock. Approving — move to squash-merge once staging run completes.
